newsitem.title: UK: BRITISH MPS ACCUSE AUSTRALIAN CRICKETERS OF SNUB.
newsitem.headline: BRITISH MPS ACCUSE AUSTRALIAN CRICKETERS OF SNUB.

text.p: British MPs have accused Australian cricketers, currently touring England to battle for the game's most coveted trophy, of snubbing their invitation to a buffet lunch.
Only one player -- wicketkeeper Ian Healy -- turned up to the event organised by parliament's All-Party Cricket Committee whose members include former Prime Minister John Major.
Seventeen MPs from all parties signed a parliamentary motion on Thursday "noting with regret" the absence of Australia's other stars from the event in parliament.
"There is no doubt that honourable members will be strengthened in their desire to see England regain the Ashes," the motion, not intended for debate, said.
Australia and England are halfway through a series of six "Ashes tests" -- international matches between the world's first two cricketing nations.
With both countries having won one game and with one drawn, the fourth test began at Headingley, northern England on Thursday, but was held up by rain.
